text.p: Intel Corp's announcement that third quarter sales will be better than expected is seen as positive for the personal computer industry.
"This suggests the PC industry is quite healthy," said analyst Charles Boucher of UBS securities.

With Intel's near monopoly of the market for microprocessors used in PCs, Intel is a bellwether for the PC industry, analysts say. If it has strong sales one month, it's reasonable to expect PC makers will have strong sales in months to follow.

Intel's revised forecast Monday that revenues will grow about five percent from the previous quarter's $4.62 billion rather than be flat as it once expected, affirms recent evidence that PC sales are starting to burgeon, analysts said.
Intel's stock price shot up 3-3/8 to 92 in after hours trading following the company's news announcement, traders said. During market hours, Intel shares rose 1/2 to 88-5/8.
"It's not only very positive for Intel, but it is supportive of other semiconductor stocks with sizable PC exposure," said PaineWebber Inc's John Lazlo. "It filters through the whole PC chain."
Many analysts revised their earnings estimates for Intel's quarter and year late Monday following the announcement.

Lazlo increased his third quarter estimate to $1.26 a share from $1.09 previously and said he expects a six percent quarter to quarter revenue gain to $4.9 billion. That would be an 18 percent revenue gain year over year.
Lazlo said Intel's forecasted revenue gain is "indeed impressive since industry revenues are estimated to decline seven or eight percent" for the year.

Boucher of UBS said he is raising his third quarter estimate to $1.20 or $1.22 a share from $1.15 a share previously and is raising his fourth quarter earnings estimate to $1.32 a share from $1.22 previously.

Analysts' consensus for the quarter had been $1.14 a share before the company's announcement, according to First Call Corp. In the year ago third quarter, Intel made $1.05 a share on revenues of $4.17 billion. The earnings included a one-time $0.03 a share gain.
Analysts said recent comments from PC makers such as Compaq Computer Corp and Dell Computer Corp, and from distributors showed signs of a pick-up.

"We certainly have been hearing the same out of the PC industry - for instance hearing from PC resellers that demand for corporate PCs is very strong - but we were not sure Intel revenues would be up this quarter," Boucher said.

Analyst Jon Joseph of Montgomery Securities Inc also said that prices of microprocessors in the gray market - or the market customers turn to if their contracted orders are less than they need - had recently spiked higher than contract prices.
Still, he said Intel's words are a great affirmation because of the rarity of Intel pre-announcing a quarter.
"They haven't done this in four years," he said.
Intel itself would not provide details of why it appears sales would be stronger than earlier expected.

Spokesman Tom Waldrop said that in general sales of microprocessors for the rest of the year are being bouyed by a move among corporations to upgrade their PCs to Pentium based systems and by an array of interesting new products in the software and appliance areas in the home market.
